questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write a good job application and CV
Problems with unpaid internships for young people
The history of the London stock exchange and banks
Why living and renting in London is so expensive
questions.why: Sam and Rob discuss internships and the problems of working for free.

questions.q: What work experience did Rob have before his first job?
options: A year-long paid internship at a bank
An unpaid job in a London office
A day or two watching how companies worked
None at all, he started work straight away
questions.why: He says he did a day or two at some companies, just shadowing.

questions.q: What are some companies accused of?
options: Using students and graduates as cheap or free workers
Refusing to hire graduates without work experience
Paying interns more than their regular full-time staff
Offering internships that are far too short to be useful
questions.why: Rob says some companies are accused of using them as cheap or free labour.

questions.q: According to James Turner, what is now expected in many careers?
options: A master's degree from a top university
Experience of working abroad for a year
A recommendation letter from a teacher
An internship before the first full-time job
questions.why: He says it's almost an expectation that a young person does an internship first.

questions.q: Why are unpaid internships bad for social mobility?
options: Interns don't learn any skills that are useful later
People who can't afford to work for free are excluded
Companies stop hiring older workers with experience
They take too long to finish, often more than a year
questions.why: Turner says unpaid internships rule out those who can't afford to work for free.

questions.q: Could Sam afford an unpaid internship in London?
options: Yes, easily, because he earns a good salary
Only for a short time, perhaps a few weeks
Yes, but only with some help from his family
No, he can hardly afford to live there already
questions.why: Sam says he can barely afford to live in London as it is.

questions.q: What other problem with internships does James Turner mention?
options: They're often only open to people with contacts in the job
They are only offered in big cities like London
Interns have to work very long hours with no breaks
Companies don't advertise them online or in newspapers
questions.why: He says they're too often open to those with established connections in the professions.

questions.q: Why does Sam mention a father who plays golf with the CEO?
options: To give some practical advice about networking at events
To joke about his own father's terrible golf skills
As an example of a family link that can help you get in
To show that most CEOs enjoy sport in their free time
questions.why: He uses it to explain how a well-connected family can 'open doors'.
